source_text: Tawnr igitur ostensiones cum sint, non oportet adhuc quzerere apud alios yeritatem, quam facile est ab Ecclesia sumere ; cum Apostoli, quasi in depositorium dives, plenissime in eam contulerint omnia que sint veritatis: uti omnis quicunque velit, sumat ex ea potum vitee. Hee est enim vitze introitus; omnes autem reliqui fures sunt et latrones. Propter quod oportet devitare quidem illos; que autem sunt Ecclesiz, cum summa diligentia diligere, et apprehendere veritatis traditionem. Quid enim? Et si de aliqua modica queestione disceptatio esset, nonne oporteret in antiquissimas recurrere ecclesias, in quibus Apostoli conversati sunt, et ab eis de presenti quastione sumere quod certum et re liquidum est? Quid autem si neque Apostoli quidem Scripturas reliquissent nobis, nonne oportebat ordinem sequi_ traditionis, quam tradiderunt iis quibus committebant ecclesias? Cui ordinationi assentiunt multze gentes barbarorum eorum qui in Christum credunt, sine charta vel atramento scriptam habentes per Spiritum in cordibus suis salutem, et veterem traditionem diligenter custodientes, in unum Deum credentes fabricatorem cceli et terree, et omnium quz in eis sunt, per Christum Jesum Dei Filium. Qui propter eminentissimam erga figmentum suum dilectionem, eam que esset ex Virgine generationem sustinuit, ipse per se hominem adunans Deo, et passus sub Pontio Pilato, et resurgens, et in claritate receptus, in gloria venturus Salvator eorum qui salvantur, et judex eorum qui judicantur, et mittens in ignem sternum transfiguratores veritatis, et contemtores Patris sui et adventus ejus. Hane fidem qui sine literis crediderunt, quantum ad sermonem nostrum, barbari sunt: quantum autem ad sententiam, et consuetudinem, et conversationem, propter fidem perquam sapientissimi sunt, et placent Deo, conversantes in omni justitia et castitate et sapientia. Quibus si aliquis annuntiaverit ea que ab hereticis adinventa sunt, proprio sermone eorum colloquens, statim concludentes aures longo longius fugient, ne audire quidem sustinentes blasphemum colloquium. | Sie per illam veterem stolorum traditionem, ne in conceptionem quidem mentis admittunt, quodcunque eorum portentiloquium est, neque enim congregatio fuit apud eos, neque doctrina instituta. 2. Ante Valentinum enim non fuerunt, qui sunt a Valentino; neque ante Marcionem erant, qui sunt a Marcione; neque omnino erant reliqui sensus maligni, quos supra enumeravimus, initiatores et inventores perversitatis eorum fierent. Valentinus enim venit Romam sub Hygino; Pio, et prorogavit tempus usque ad Anicetum. Oerdon autem qui ante Marcionem, et hic sub Hygino, qui fuit octavus episcopus, seepe in ecclesiam veniens, et exhomologesin faciens, sic consummavit, modo quidem latenter docens, modo vero exhomologesin faciens, modo vero ab aliquibus traductus in his que docebat male, et abstentus est a religiosorum hominum conventu. 3. Marcion autem illi succedens invaluit sub Aniceto, !}decimum locum episcopatus continente. Reliqui vero qui vocantur Gnostici, a Menandro Simonis discipulo, quemadmodum ostendimus, accipientes initia, unusquisque eorum, cujus participatus est sententiz, ejus et pater, et antistes apparuit. Omnes autem hi multo posterius, mediantibus jam Ecclesize temporibus, insurrexerunt in suam apostasiam.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, since these are demonstrations, it is not necessary to seek truth from others, which is easy to take from the Church; since the Apostles, as if into a rich repository, have fully conferred all things of truth into it: so that whoever wishes may take from it the drink of life. For this is the entrance of life; all the rest, however, are thieves and robbers. On account of which it is necessary to avoid them; but those things which are of the Church, with the greatest diligence to love and to seize the tradition of truth. For what reason? And if there were a dispute about some small question, would it not be necessary to recur to the most ancient churches, in which the Apostles conversed, and from them to take concerning the present question what is certain and clear? What, however, if the Apostles had not even left writings to us, would it not be necessary to follow the order of tradition, which they handed down to those to whom they entrusted the churches? To which ordination many barbarian nations, who believe in Christ, assent, having salvation written in their hearts by the Spirit without paper or ink, and diligently preserving the old tradition, believing in one God, the maker of heaven and earth and all things that are in them, through Christ Jesus, the Son of God. Who, on account of the most excellent love towards His creature, sustained the generation which was from the Virgin, Himself gathering man to God, and having suffered under Pontius Pilate, and having risen, and having been received in glory, is about to come in glory as the Savior of those who are saved, and as the judge of those who are judged, and sending into eternal fire the corrupters of truth and the despisers of His Father and His advent. These who have believed without writings, as far as our speech is concerned, are barbarians: but as far as judgment and custom and conversation are concerned, on account of faith they are most wise and pleasing to God, living in all justice and chastity and wisdom. To whom if someone should announce those things which have been invented by heretics, speaking in their own language, immediately closing their ears they will flee far away, not even enduring to hear the blasphemous conversation. Thus, through that old tradition of the elders, they do not even admit into the conception of the mind whatever their portentous speech is, nor was there a gathering or established doctrine among them. For before Valentinus, those who are from Valentinus were not; nor before Marcion were those who are from Marcion; nor were there at all the remaining malignant senses, which we enumerated above, to become the initiators and inventors of their perversity. For Valentinus came to Rome under Hyginus; and he prolonged his time until Anicetus. But Cerdo, who was before Marcion, and this one under Hyginus, who was the eighth bishop, coming often into the church and making confession, thus completed, sometimes teaching secretly, sometimes making confession, sometimes being handed over by some to those things which he taught badly, and was absent from the gathering of religious men. And Marcion, succeeding him, prevailed under Anicetus, holding the tenth place of the episcopate. The rest, however, who are called Gnostics, receiving their beginnings from Menander, the disciple of Simon, as we have shown, each one of them, whose sentiment he has participated in, has appeared as his father and bishop. All these, however, much later, with the times of the Church intervening, have risen up into their own apostasy.
pass_b_english: Since these demonstrations exist, you need not seek the truth from others, for it is easy to obtain from the Church. The Apostles, like men depositing a treasure in a rich repository, fully entrusted all things that belong to the truth to her, so that anyone who wishes may draw from her the drink of life. This is the entrance to life; all the rest are thieves and robbers (John 10:1, 9–10). Therefore you must avoid them, but you must love and lay hold of the things that belong to the Church with the greatest diligence, seizing the tradition of the truth. For what reason? Even if a dispute should arise over some minor question, would it not be necessary to resort to the most ancient churches with which the Apostles held intercourse, and to take from them what is certain and clear regarding the present question? And what if the Apostles had not even left writings to us? Would it not then be necessary to follow the order of the tradition which they handed down to those to whom they entrusted the churches? To this ordering many nations of barbarians who believe in Christ give their assent. They have salvation written in their hearts by the Spirit, without paper or ink (2 Cor 3:3), and they diligently preserve the ancient tradition. They believe in one God, the Maker of heaven and earth and of all things that are in them, through Christ Jesus, the Son of God (Gen 1:1; Acts 14:15). He, because of His surpassing love for His creature, endured the birth from the Virgin, Himself uniting man to God. He suffered under Pontius Pilate, rose again, was received up in glory, and will come in glory as the Savior of those who are saved and the Judge of those who are judged (Acts 1:11; 2 Tim 4:1). He will send into eternal fire the corrupters of the truth and the despisers of His Father and of His coming (Matt 25:41; 2 Thess 1:8–9). Those who have believed without writings are, as far as our speech goes, barbarians; but as far as judgment, custom, and conduct go, they are exceedingly wise because of their faith, and they please God, living in all righteousness, chastity, and wisdom (James 3:13; 1 Pet 2:12). If anyone should announce to them the things invented by heretics, speaking in their own tongue, they will immediately stop their ears and flee far away, not even enduring to hear the blasphemous talk. Thus, through that ancient tradition of the elders, they do not admit into the conception of their mind whatever portentous speech the heretics utter, for there was no assembly among them, nor was there any established doctrine.

For before Valentinus, those who are from Valentinus did not exist; nor before Marcion did those who are from Marcion exist; nor were the remaining malignant opinions, which we enumerated above, in existence at all to become the originators and inventors of their perversity. Valentinus came to Rome under Hyginus and prolonged his time until Anicetus. But Cerdo, who preceded Marcion, appeared under Hyginus, who was the eighth bishop. He often came into the church and made confession, thus completing his course—sometimes teaching secretly, sometimes making confession, sometimes being reproved by some for the things he taught badly—and he abstained from the assembly of religious men. Marcion, succeeding him, flourished under Anicetus, who held the tenth place of the episcopate. The rest who are called Gnostics received their beginnings from Menander, the disciple of Simon, as we have shown. Each one of them, whose opinion he has shared, has appeared as his father and bishop. All these, however, arose much later, in the midst of the Church's times, rising up into their own apostasy.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with appropriate scripture citations (John 10:1, 9–10; 2 Cor 3:3; Gen 1:1; Acts 14:15; Acts 1:11; 2 Tim 4:1; Matt 25:41; 2 Thess 1:8–9; James 3:13; 1 Pet 2:12) which correspond to the theological content of the Latin clauses. All nuances regarding the historical figures (Hyginus, Anicetus, Valentinus, Marcion, Menander) and the description of the 'barbarian' nations are preserved.
